startup.name: Evident Machines
startup.one_liner: Real-world benchmarks and RL environments for electrical engineering
startup.description: Benchmarks and reinforcement learning environments for AI doing real electrical engineering, covering design, simulation and physical experiments in an SF lab. The experiments become training data and environments sold to frontier AI labs. Two people, San Francisco, Fall 2026.

yc_acceptance.basis: Blind test: the company is already accepted to YC for its batch, so the acceptance estimate is a placeholder near certainty rather than a forecast. The unconditional prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent, third party figures in yc_acceptance.md).
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable in this test because the company was accepted. Had it been assessed as an applicant, the most plausible reason for a no would be a tiny team in a crowded RL environment market with a capital heavy lab. The founders would also need to show in the interview that they can ship quickly and have a specific first customer in mind, since YC weighs team speed and clear user need over market size.

Frontier labs buy environments but have many vendors and in house teams, and a two person company with a physical lab has high cost per task. Klavis recorded only 500K and Sherpa Labs only 500K, so a round above that needs a signed lab customer or a standout benchmark.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B needs a product beyond bespoke data, such as a standard benchmark that labs license annually. The likely stop is that the RL environment market commoditises, buyers consolidate, and the physical lab model does not scale like software environments. The analogs in the records suggest only a minority of companies in this cohort that reach a seed ever reach this round, and the company would need clear paying customers and improving margins to be among them.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C needs a platform position. Likely the company ends as a services style data vendor or is acquired by a lab or a data company, since no vendor of this type has reached C in the YC records. The records show very few comparable companies reaching this stage, and those that did had durable revenue and a defensible position, which this company would need to show well before then.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stalls as a niche data vendor or is absorbed. The buyers are a handful of frontier labs that can switch or build in house, and many RL environment startups chase the same budgets. Analogs such as Klavis, Sherpa Labs and Refresh show small recorded rounds and no verified later raises.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building valid benchmarks that link simulation to physical measurements needs electrical engineering depth and lab equipment. A two person team can start with narrow tasks.

takeover_risk.rationale: Data vendors can add an electrical engineering domain with expert hires, but physical experiments are harder to copy. A well resourced rival would need roughly the stated time and would have the incentive if the category proves valuable.

narrative.headline: A narrow but timely hardware benchmark and RL environment vendor that can likely raise a seed and then must prove labs keep paying.
narrative.general_summary: Evident Machines sells electrical engineering benchmarks and RL environments to frontier labs. RL environment startups drew many small seeds in 2025 and buyer concentration is the main danger. The physical lab is a differentiator and a cost. The ladder sits near the B2B anchors with a higher seed because lab budgets are large and the founders can sell a narrow dataset quickly. The estimates are anchored on the 2023 to 2025 B2B cohort and adjusted only with the stated reasons, keeping each step within 0.75 times its anchor. Reaching a later round years after the batch is common for companies with paying customers, and a pivot followed by a raise is part of the upside band, so the ladder asks whether a round is reached and not how fast.

assumptions: Blind test: only the batch input file and market web searches were used; no company specific records. The seed step is read as a round above the standard YC deal of about 500K dollars within roughly 12 months of batch start.

Extraction coverage is 662 of 6,399 companies researched in the calibration sample, plus recent cohort records; later cohorts are right censored, so base rates for 2023 to 2025 batches understate eventual progress.
